provenance: The tools a delegated worker calls BY NAME through the one MCP the gateway serves — named here rather than left to the server prefix because a tool the model must first search for is a round trip where turns stall. It began as the measured union of the tools real workers called across 45 sessions and grows by argument, not measurement, where a missing verb makes the wrong behaviour: the write side of a workspace (`workspace_write`, `workspace_delete`, `workspace_move`, `entity_upsert`, `fetch_asset`), the membership acts the front page queues on a chat, and the claim book the desk cards ask for. Every name is one the edge serves on a full deployment except `open_page` and `workspace_target`, the two verbs the harness turns into panel and focus events (Vexa-ai/vexa#1586, #1611), which only the dogfood rig serves today and no product prompt names; `tests/test_prompt_tools_served.py` holds the list to exactly that.
why_declared_here: This is the worker's least-privilege boundary, and until now its provenance was a measurement document in the dogfood LANE (`deploy/dogfood/rig/TOOL-USAGE.md`) — so the boundary could not be reviewed, or shipped, without a directory that merges on a different schedule. A domain's allow-list is the domain's.
degrades_in_both_directions: A tool the server does not serve is inert in an allow-set, so this list ageing behind the server costs nothing; a tool the server gains and this list lacks is still permitted by the server prefix on the first line of the allow-set.
